text:
Cale Makar came back from a stretch out of the lineup on Wednesday and picked up three assists in a 6-0 win over Montreal, then won Friday's game in Minnesota in a shootout after the Avalanche came back from three goals down. Welcome back.

The scoring is absurd even by his standards: 27 points in 21 games, 22 of them assists, and 16 points in his last ten. That pace, 3.39 points per 60 minutes, sits above the range our numbers think is sustainable for him (about 2.2 to 2.9), so some cooling is the honest expectation. Even cooled, he's on track for something like 74 to 99 points.

What's not luck: he still drives the play. Colorado gets 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, he has the hardest shot in the league by NHL EDGE's measure (101.9 mph), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 97th percentile among defensemen for setting up shots last season. Evolving-Hockey notes he plays with strong teammates, which flatters the raw numbers a little. Watch his minutes: he played 27 on Friday.
